newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by adequate hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
"We had a pretty good run and have what we need for Thursday's kill," a southern Minnesota packer hog buyer said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts Tuesday ran 7,000 head over the 100,000 estimate, according to USDA statistics, and were seen meeting or exceeding Wednesday's estimate of 100,000, several dealers said.
Top price for hogs delivered to the plant in the interior Iowa/southern Minnesota area was seen at $60.00, they said.

Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $59.50 to $60.00 and Indiana/Ohio top values for hogs delivered to plants were seen $60.00 to $60.50. Hog marketings expanded amid cooler temperatures, mostly in the western corn belt, and higher cash hog prices Monday and Tuesday, sources said.
"There were a lot of areas where hogs were over $60.00, and that was not going to slow them down," said Dave Maher, livestock analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.
Maher added that rainfall in Iowa and Illinois cooled temperatures to the low and mid-80s (Fahrenheit) from mid-90s and allowed farmers to move a "few more" hogs.
Extreme heat and humidity on Monday and early Tuesday limited marketings as farmers refrained from shipping too many hogs because of possible increased stress and death-loss.
